text: Cut to the chase-I may have just had the best meal so far in over a year in Nashville. Now back to the beginning. The Old School Farm is so much more than a restaurant, make it a destination and plan on relaxing, unwinding and sitting a spell. After all, you didn't take the drive out in the country to hurry things, now did you? We arrived early on a Friday, and made our way into the bar for a flight of ciders. They have several local beers on tap as well as Guinness, along with the above mentioned ciders. The wine list looked extensive and they're crafting some very inventive house made cocktails. We sampled the Bloody Mary with house made tomato juice bursting with the flavor of the garden. They have a beautiful large bar room with stage for live music and tables to dine here besides the main dining room. Since they weren't yet busy we could engage with the staff and learn more about the wonderful program the Old School Farm supports as well as their bee keeping endeavors. The menu changes weekly depending on what's fresh from the garden and the local farms. We decided on three plates to share. A roasted eggplant dip with grilled flatbread, roasted baby beets over yogurt drizzled with their local honey, and the shining star- sweet corn ricotta tortellini with pea shoots and soft boiled quail egg with chili oil. One bite of the tortellini and we both declared it the best pasta we can remember having. We finished our meal with a dessert of deconstructed grasshopper pie. Every plate was a winner. While we were dining the jazz quartet added to the ambience. We took time to walk the property, admiring their gardens, chicken coops and bee hives. It looks like they have an open air building that would be perfect for weddings or events. A visit here is so much more than just a meal, it's an experience worth taking your time to explore.
llm_rationale: No description of illness, contamination, or unsafe food handling.

text: I have eaten here several times over the last few months up to the week that the restaurant opened in the Winter. The first 2 or 3 times service was exceptional. It was easy to find what I could have on the menu that was gluten free. I was told all of the mole's are gluten free and most of the menu was gluten free with exception to some fried items and desert items. I was even told they had a dedicated fryer for the whole fish and it did not contain anything that had gluten. I was so happy and impressed with that. The food was great, there hasn't been one thing on the menu that I did not like, but the fried fish, elotes, and stuffed peppers remains my favorite items on the menu. Now, the last time I dined in it wasn't even busy because it was raining, our waitress had a major attitude with me in particular because I had a gluten allergy. She was rolling her eyes and talking under her breath and basically acting like she did not want to serve us at all. She never even returned to the table except to bring us our bill and she had charged us for food we didn't even order. We were so disappointed in service that night. There were questions about whether the once dedicated fryer was contaminated with gluten and if it was safe to order certain items. Then I was told nothing could be guaranteed to be contamination free wheres all the other times I dined in the staff and management was fairly confident that their kitchen could provide gluten free food. Of all the times I ate there this was the only time I was served food that tested positive for gluten and no one knew why. It was an extremely disappointing service and I left with having barely eaten anything. The situation was further exasperated by the rude waitress. We ended up paying the whole check (even the food we didn't order) and just left because we were tired of waiting for our waitress to come around to tell her about the extra items charged to us. With that being said, prior to these events I would have rated this restaurant five stars because parking is easy- they have valet and free street parking. The restaurant is nice and its got a nice design, decor, and nice rooftop bar. The food & drinks are great and fairly priced and the staff was exceptional and friendly- all except the one time. Now... I am not even sure if I can safely eat there which is obviously important if you have Celiacs. So, I can't say its even Celiac safe as I could before. That last experience may have been a one off, I am unsure, but 2 of the 4 times I ate there there were questions of if the dedicated fryer had been used to cook other items containing wheat.
llm_rationale: The reviewer's food tested positive for gluten, despite their previous experiences with the restaurant's gluten-free protocols.

text: If you have celiac disease or a gluten sensitivity I HIGHLY recommend avoiding this place at all costs. My cousin and I both have celiac disease and went there last night. I ordered fish tacos and she ordered a chicken salad. I checked online about my meal and all ingredients listed were gluten free (I was mainly concerned with the sauce on the fish since I knew the tortillas were corn and the toppings were salad- all gluten free things). My cousin TOLD the waitress she was gluten free and couldn't eat gluten and the waitress said "I got you". She ordered chicken and salad. When my tacos came out they were fried in flour- does not say fried on the menu but that's fine. I sent them back and apologized for not asking further questions but explained I too have celiac disease and can't have flour and I asked if I could reorder what my cousin was eating since hers looked good and was gluten free. The waitress then says hers was not gluten free and says she didn't hear my cousin say that. My cousin had all but finished her plate by that time so it was only a matter of time before she was sick. She brought out my dinner which was chicken and salad and my chicken was made differently than my cousins was (without soy sauce). And it was really just okay. I understand this establishment doesn't claim to be gluten free. However when someone says they are, PAY ATTENTION. Especially since they do offer gluten free items upon request and she said "I got you" as if it wouldn't be an issue. It's a food allergy. Which can kill you over time so it's extremely important to listen. Drinks were good and service overall was decent. I hate that the waitress didn't pay attention though and then tried to say she wasn't told about the allergy when she was- we all heard. Won't be back due to this, which is unfortunate because it seemed like a cool place. If you don't have celiac disease it seems like a good place though!
llm_rationale: Waitress failed to pay attention to gluten-free request and served contaminated food.

text: I'm taking J.B. Dawson's up a star and 1/2, for a few good reasons. First of all they make an awesome lemon drop or dirty martini and they are huge and powerful, yes and only $7.00, but do plan on hitting the sack after you've had one of these babies. J.B. Dawson's mailed us a $15.00 gift card for no good reason, to be used when you spent $25.00 or more in food, so hey, why not? I'm glad we did, even though we spent a good $80.00, we were really quite pleased. The baked potato soup was awesome this time, creamy and loaded with crispy bacon and cheddar cheese and I had seen the lump crab cakes scattered all over the menu and after inquiring and Shannon telling us they were pretty well pure lump and backfin, I opted to do the four mini crab cakes appetizer. They had a bit more filler in than I like, but they were still loaded with crab meat, peppers and spices, very good indeed and the bonus was a dill sauce served on the side which really complimented them. These were not little balls either they were larger than I had anticipated. We also ordered the cajun shrimp appetizer because I am an appetizer whore and it was enough to be a meal with eight large shrimp, cajun coated and grilled and served on top of two thick slices of grilled garlic bread with a side garlic butter dipping sauce, something you could make at home easily, but it was still very good and gave me a new idea for a quick fix. For my entree, yes, I have to have it all, I ordered the jumbo lump crab linguine alfredo! Hello, loaded with lump crab meat and the portion was huge, the linguine was cooked to perfection and the sauce was delightful, it's been a long time since I've had alfredo and it was a nice change of pace. Listen to what hubby had! Monday's only, all you can eat baby back ribs with a salad of your choice and unlimited house or premium sides, $24.95! He choose the caesar and they do have anchovy filet's and extra shaved parmesan cheese, he added red onion and I ate half of it, shhh, no sharing is allowed on the all you can eat deals and no take home bags, even though we did... We had a very long and tiring weekend with a wedding and a birthday party and we were both hungry, yet exhausted, so he did not even finish one rack and I had scarfed two of those bones. The ribs were outstanding, seriously perfectly seasoned, the sauce was very tasty, the ribs were beyond tender and meaty! He could have had twelve or more different sides be he only asked for the cole slaw, which was fresh and a large portion, garlic mashed for me and their fries rock, delightful little shoestrings of potato fried to a golden brown. We ended up taking most of the food home and have another good meal out of it, I would not hesitate after this last experience to pay J.B. Dawson's another visit, especially with all of the new restaurants opening up and so many others closing down and what constitutes a chain to the other reviewers? There are four J.B. Dawson's well scattered, it's not like they are a factory or something and the food and service is good and their martinis kick butt!. Oh and hey gluten free friends, they have an extensive menu just for you, including pastas!
llm_rationale: No description of illness, contamination, or unsafe food handling.

text: Finding a good restaurant with vegan options in a new town can be difficult. Siam Elephant was intriguing and within walking distance from our hotel, so we decided to give it a try. We alerted the waiter that I had a peanut allergy in addition to my vegan diet, and asked if any dishes could be altered to suit me. The waiter told us that they could practically do anything, and we went on with our order. He was very helpful while we ordered, as he listed each non-vegan ingredient in each dish and asked us if we wanted to substitute or take it out. The overall ordering experience was pleasant, as he was very thorough in making sure we knew what each dish contained. When the food arrived, the true test began. I had seen reviews about the restaurant being insensitive to allergies, which worried me. Whenever I consume any food I am allergic to, I immediately get a reaction. Ready to grab my epi-pen, I took my first bite of the Spicy Noodle dish... And I let out a huge sigh of relief. The foods were exactly as we had ordered. Everything was vegan, meat subbed with tofu, with no trace of a peanut in sight. Confident in the food, I dug in and devoured most of the meal. The actual flavors of the food were delicious. Everything was well-balanced and seasoned nicely. The Spicy Noodle dish was delicious with the mix of hot rice noodles and bell peppers. The special at the time, Tempura Avocado, was also delicious and I'd recommend to anyone that likes avocados to snatch it if available. The Coconut soup was also extremely good, not to mention the overall presentation. Pro Tip for vegans/lactose intolerants: the Thai Tea Boba comes with half-and-half. However, just alert the waiter about your veganism/intolerance and ask to sub for coconut milk. Tastes just as good! Overall, the experience here was gosh-darn amazing and it would be my first choice if I ever returned. I recommend it to anybody, as there are so many versatile options that the waiters are willing to tweak.
llm_rationale: Reviewer had a severe peanut allergy but did not experience any adverse reaction after alerting the waiter and receiving a safe meal.

text: Disability Accomodations at the Royal Senesta Hotel, New Orleans. June 2011 Disabilities come in all shapes and sizes. Most people think in terms of the well known and visible conditions, such as mobility issues, deafness, blindness... But there are many more little known conditions that are just as devastating for a normal life. Getting accommodations for these is often a tough and frustrating battle. The Royal Senesta Hotel of New Orleans, and in particular, the Director of Guest Relations, Katherine Jolivette, took the opposite tack. Before we even arrived, they went above and beyond my expectations in trying to create a safe place for me. Upon our arrival Katherine personally met us in the lobby and took us up to a room that had been specially prepared, went over the steps they had taken and asked if there was anything MORE they could do. I travel quite a lot, and have never seen a hospitality staff this hands on and attentive to detail. She acted like I was the only person she needed to be concerned about, taking as much time as needed, and never made me feel rushed or like an inconvenience. I found out later in the evening that she was also coordinating three weddings that day! Because my condition is relatively rare, I explained what I could about it and gave her a website where she could find out more, if she wanted. Usually when I do this, I imagine the person just tosses it as soon as I'm out of sight, however Katherine went to the site and actually read it through, asking me more questions about it next time she saw me. I have a very severe allergy to a very common substance, Latex. This is so severe that the amount needed to cause an anaphylactic reaction is measured in micrograms. A microgram is 1,000th of a milligram, in case you were wondering. And anaphylaxis means, essentially, death measured in minutes without intervention. In my first twenty four hours in NOLA, I had already suffered three anaphylactic events. Fortunately, I carry a pharmacy of intervention medicines with me at all times or I wouldn't be writing this. Trying to find a hotel willing to accommodate this is a nightmare. At the Royal Senesta, the reservation desk took the time to check all the possible sources of contamination and reported back that the hotel food service and restaurants were clear, and that although the housekeeping staff normally uses latex gloves, they had appropriate alternatives for our room. They did this all before we actually made the reservation. Reservation made, Katherine arranged for us to be in an upgraded room for the same price because it was isolated from the other hotel rooms where latex might be used. To my surprise, we were moved a couple days later to a newly available room with easy access to fresh air when needed to help relieve the asthma attacks I was having from multiple surprise encounters with latex in New Orleans. I never asked for the room change, she simply saw that I was having difficulty and made the necessary arrangements. She continued to check in with me, by phone and every time we passed in the hotel, to make sure things were going well. I really can't think of enough words to commend this kind of superlative service. In addition to my severe allergy issues, my husband is blind. He also had a wonderful customer experience. All the staff, from housekeeping, to the restaurant and food service, to the front desk and porters were friendly, cheerful, and always ready to help if needed. Of note, none of them over compensated in that annoying let-me-do-everything-for-you caretaking way that drives us who are disabled nuts. I would recommend this hotel to anyone with special needs without hesitation. If you are clear about what you need, I have no doubt that Katherine and her staff will find a way to make things work for you.
llm_rationale: Review describes exceptional service and accommodations for disabilities, but no food safety hazards.

text: We have tried Fiamme twice: once dining in and once with carry out. Dining in was March 2021. There are half a dozen tables inside and they are in extremely close quarters. My husband and I are not particularly concerned about COVID precautions, but if you are someone who is, the set up would likely be a turn-off for you. Part of the reason we had gone to Fiamme was because of their advertisements mentioning they have vegan and gluten-free options. When we asked our server about these options, he seemed stunned, like we had just asked what color he thought our auras were. He took our drink orders and left us to investigate on our own. Luckily, after reading more into the menu, we were able to navigate to Fiamme's gluten-free and vegan options without our server's assistance. Service was slow and our server seemed confused and/or possibly inebriated. We enjoyed the food when it finally arrived. Once our food came we never saw our server again. After about 30 minutes I went to the front counter and asked for the check. The second time we ordered pick up in April 2021. The pies were ready on time. The server who took my payment and gave me the pies spent most of the time I was interacting with him yelling at another server he was working with. It made me uncomfortable but I was in and out of there quickly. Again, food tasted good. After our first visit, I came down with some gnarly food poisoning (fever, stomach cramps, intestinal distress). I generally have an iron stomach and I think associating food poisoning with a business is generally a jerk move. BUT, after our second visit, my husband came down with the exact same symptoms, which leads me to believe this may be an actual risk of eating at Fiamme. Between the sub-par service and our post-food-consumption experiences on both visits, we will not be returning to Fiamme. Which is a bummer, as it is a legit pizza experience.

text: Bar Louie protects customers from unprotected servers by ignoring older patrons Due to Covid, I chose mid-afternoon for a RARE and relished venture out. Arrival time, 3:11 ish. Upon getting an IPA, I said I'd hang for a while, before ordering another drink and a burger. The while grew long enough to hang a herd of elephants, as my now-empty beer glass grew warm for about 19 minutes after I finished. Even the persistent gnats gave up. Then, I heard another server say, "Your friends are here." There he was! Finally! He burst through the inside/outside door, inches past my table, to engage in playful banter with his friends,...I knew he'd at long, last notice me, wide anxious eyes, drooling. Twenty-one additional minutes passed. TWENTY-ONE. That's a peace sign and one finger. I got up to retrieve napkins to soak up the sweat from my water in a ploy to get his attention. Wimpy, I know, but a "gentle reminder." It was better than apologizing for interrupting him. Yes? No? Still, no nod, no acknowledgement from three tables away, with no humans in between, much less 15 feet to the right and ten feet to the left. With all that time I had on my hands, I began to think--instead of eat and drink--and studied his mask. It hung just on top of his upper lip, leaving his protruding proboscis for all to see. Would he sneeze? Was he contaminating the food he wasn't taking orders for or wasn't serving? As my impatience grew, I slowly got grossed out. What if a drip from his nose contaminates my order? Maybe this was God's grace in keeping me from getting the Covid-19 virus by a server who saves people by ignoring them. Carmel, Indiana's Bar Louie, so convenient, so inviting for someone who had not left home much since March 23, 2020, such a thrill to be out...saved me today by treating me like "The Invisible Woman." GREY LIVES MATTER. Side Dish: My magical spell of invisibility dissolved when I ordered dinner at Bub's Burgers.

text: ***This is more of a 3.5 place but I rounded up*** Okay, so I was in Nashville last weekend for a friend's bachelorette party. For our first night in town, we came here for dinner. I'll start by saying that the building itself is super swanky. It looked small from the outside but once inside, it grew into a really lovely dining area. It looked as though there were some fireplace features that could have been really pretty but those were turned off. It was FREEZING in the restaurant. It was in the 80s outside but dreadfully cold inside which always puts a damper on any dining experience for me but I powered through. Okay, drinks: pass on the cocktails. They sound good but they're small and feel watered down. They have a great wine selection so I'd recommend going that route unless you're inclined to have a glutenous beer. For food, the maid of honor ordered a charcuterie board. She specified that she needed to have the crackers on a separate plate because she has celiac's disease and any cross-contamination of gluten could cause her to be sick. They brought everything out together on one plate anyway which was disappointing but our waiter made it right by bringing out a whole new charcuterie board sans crackers. The cheese and meats were loved by all in my group. It was a perfect appetizer. They also bring out a really good bread that has great seasoning and is perfectly baked. For my meal, I ordered the swordfish which is one of their daily specials. It was very good except super salty. I wish they had toned down the seasonings a little. Otherwise I really enjoyed it and I believe my friends also really enjoyed their meals. We were disappointed a bit with our server who seemed to disappear for long periods of time. We ordered 2nd drinks before our meals came out and didn't receive them until after our plates were cleared away :( Not cool. So then we had to stay there longer than we wanted in order to drink the drinks we wanted to have with our meals. Overall, I'd say this place was a roller coaster ride for our group. Some things were fantastic and other things were pretty bad. I come to Nashville fairly regularly since I have a lot of family and friends in the area so I may come back and see if things have shaped up to make good on my four stars!
llm_rationale: The restaurant failed to accommodate a customer's gluten allergy by serving gluten-containing crackers on the same plate as gluten-free items.

No one who has had food sensitivities for very long would expect a restaurant to be fully gluten free. text: I recently went to this BJs with my boyfriend and roommate and had some issues. I have some very severe and life threatening food allergies and am very careful about telling servers about them so I don't, you know, die. This was the first time in years that I forgot to do so, but as I've eaten at this restaurant before, I knew what to avoid so I wasn't too worried (I made sure nothing I ordered had any nuts listed in the ingredients I didn't participate in the appetizers because I was unsure about the ingredients). Out comes our food and I notice something strange--almonds, or what looked like them, on my pasta. I have my boyfriend take a bite and he unfortunately confirms my suspicions. We immediately alert the server who apologized profusely and takes the pasta, bringing it back to the kitchen to be replaced. Luckily everything turned out fine, the wait staff was amazing, and I didn't end up needing to use my EpiPen. Here's the issue, though--if I had taken a bite, it is very possible that something serious may have happened to me, and I definitely would have gone to the hospital. It's not too much to ask, right? That a chef doesn't add ingredients to a dish without listing it? Because if it happened to me then it probably has happened to other people. All in all I probably won't go back, not because the food wasn't delicious or that the wait staff had any issues, but because I shouldn't have to risk serious health problems when I eat pasta.
llm_rationale: Reviewer's severe food allergy was not properly accommodated, with a potentially hazardous ingredient added to their dish.

text: I have kind of a love-hate relationship with this place. It's nice to be able to buy local produce, eggs, and other product. The competitiveness of the prices fluctuates, but they aren't terrible, and can be pretty good for products on sale. They carry a lot of things that you won't find in other stores, like locally produced gluten free bread, tofu, and other items. Sometimes the local items are prohibitively expensive ($12 bread?) and sometimes they're very competitive with nonlocal items at other stores. I really like the espresso that they sell, too, and the cheese selection is great and the prices are totally reasonable for the quality. However, the selection of many other items isn't good, even for specialty-ish products. You will find a much larger selection of dairy-free milks at Acme, for example. I think the only greek yogurt they sell is Fage, and it's much pricier than you'll find elsewhere. The prices also fluctuate more than is typical for chain stores (not sales, but the regular prices of eggs and produce and such). But those are issues that I'm going to guess are pretty typical for coops, and worth dealing with for access to the local produce and cheese. My main issue is, it is a MISERABLE shopping experience. I was skeptical of the reviews about the crowds and rude customers, thinking many of the reviewers are just used to shopping in roomy suburban locations. I don't know if I've ever seen a review for a smaller store in the city without complaints about narrow aisles and crowds and rushed, rude patrons, and usually I find that these stores are perfectly pleasant in reality. But in this case, the reviews are spot-on. The layout is such that you cannot stand still at any location in the store without blocking the circulation of the store. Even when the store is nearly empty, I feel rushed, because I am always in someone's way, just by virtue of the store layout. People will literally drive their shopping carts into you and look at you expectantly, as though fully expecting you to just go limp and allow yourself to be shoved out of the way. I would recommend you not even bother trying to shop here your first few times if you can't shop well outside peak hours (before 3:30 PM), because you can't just stand there and look over the shelf trying to find the items that you need or easily move amongst the shelves. If you do have to shop during peak hours, I would recommend that you just accept that you are going to be in everyone's way and everyone is going to be in yours, dispense with any rules of politesse, and try to get your items and get out of there as quickly as possible. This store does have a larger selection of some things than the Chestnut Hill one, especially the value-oriented items, like the bulk bins and some types of conventional produce. (I could not find non-organic berries at CH, for example.) But for more basic things that are in stock at both stores, I would highly recommend Chestnut Hill over this location. It's compact too, but the layout doesn't leave people trying to bulldoze each other out of the way of the kale.
llm_rationale: No description of illness, contamination, or unsafe food handling.

text: I'm amused at some of the other reviewers using words like,"old-fashioned" and "blue-collar food" and "no-frills." Well, guess what I want from a night out at a steakhouse -- FRILLS! As someone who has worked in over ten restaurants, I don't even know where to start with what is wrong with this place. There were nine people in our party, but they were able to seat us immediately on a Saturday night. (That was a HUGE red flag for me, but we were hungry and I was outvoted by my fellow diners.) The "menu" is printed on cheap paper placemats, a la the kiddie menu at Denny's. And at first, we were confused by the "You cook it" and "We'll cook it for you" sections, but it really is just that. If you want a steak, they bring a raw slab of meat to your table on a cracked, plain, ungarnished plate, and you have to stand over a small, filthy, crowded grill and cook it yourself. (And then, I suppose, put it back on the same plate. Pay no attention to cross-contamination issues...) When I foolishly asked the server (Maude) if I could have a steak cooked for me, she snapped that there was only one cook in the kitchen and he was very busy. Shame on me. Since I'm one of those crazy people who likes to have her food cooked for her when she goes out to a restaurant, I decided to order the salad bar, which came with bread, beans and potato. The salad bar had iceberg lettuce, cucumbers. onion, beets and carrots. Oh, and croutons. That's it. The bread was packaged, white "Texas toast" style, that you took out of the plastic bag yourself. Classy. The beans were tasteless and obviously from a can. The baked potato was wrapped very tightly with cheap, thin aluminum foil that shredded when removed. I'm embarrassed to say that it took me five minutes to get it off the spud and I still got pieces of foil stuck in my teeth. Some of my fellow diners did order rib-eyes, and said that they tasted okay, but when I went by the grill, I overheard other people asking each other how to cook their steaks and where the grill was hottest, cooler, etc. (You weren't expecting there to be anyone supervising the grill or helping out, did you?) The grill itself was covered with thick grime and charred bits of beef, and the metal shakers holding the seasonings were so old and filthy that I wouldn't have touched them if my life depended on it. Normally, I would complain if a waitress grabbed my plate from me before I was done eating, but here I let her do it. I had to ask three different people to refill our water glasses, and I left with a feeling in my gut like I'd just eaten a throw pillow. For all of the people who gave this place good reviews, do yourselves a favor and investigate other steak houses. You might find that they are cleaner and friendlier, the food isn't from a can and it is actually cooked FOR you. My 12 year-old summed it up nicely when referring to the placemat menus,cook-your-own food and lack of service: "Mom, this is the LAZIEST restaurant we've ever been to!" Yup.
llm_rationale: No described illness or contamination, only complaints about food quality and service.

That said, sushi rolls come down to rice and fish so they should be safe since both ingredients are inherently gluten free. Massive disappointment at Azie. Their version of gfree sushi is to make sushi with nasty brown rice. Apparently, the rice vinegar they use to bind the white rice together in the regular sushi contains wheat. Using these lower quality rice vinegars that contain gluten is cheaper and easier for restaurants like Azie. Azie management, I applaud your effort to offer gluten free menu items so thank you for that. I also appreciate that you are up front that the regular sushi is unsafe for those with gluten issues. But put your money where your mouth is - use higher quality ingredients so everyone can eat your sushi. What you don't understand about folks with food allergies is that they just want what everyone else is eating- they just want to eat safely. This is an EASY fix on your part but, yes, it may cost you a little extra. Then you really can say you have gluten free sushi instead of the poor substitute you currently offer.

text: Warning - I actually know what I'm talking about when it comes to Thai food. This review may offend those who don't. My parents are from Laos, whose cuisine is very similar to Thai food. We have cooked, eaten and continue to eat a lot of traditional Thai cuisine. We like to eat around town at different Thai restaurants because for us it's like going to our friend's mom's house for dinner. There is a lot of hype about the Smiling Elephant and we had an afternoon to kill so we made our trek across town to check it out. The area is an up-and-coming part of Nashville close to downtown. Trendy little shops, restaurants, and condos are popping up all over this part of town. The restaurant was small and quaint, very homely and comfortable. The employees greeted us with warm smiles as soon as we stepped in, and made sure service was exceptional throughout our lunch. Thumbs up. We ordered the fresh rolls, tofu Pad Thai with green bean noodles, and Pad Kra Pao. The fresh rolls were fresh, but we prefer ours with either shrimp or pork or both like a lot of other places give you - especially for that price. The Pad Thai was interesting. The menu says it's not like the "Americanized" Pad Thai you get at other restaurants, but maybe it should be. People read that from the menu and put it in their review like they actually know the difference between traditional and Americanized Thai food. Some might have an idea, but most - no. The low-carb green bean noodles were actually pretty good, but the dish as a whole was not satisfactory - again, especially for the price. Our other lunch entree was the Pad Kra Pao with jumbo lump crab, served with a fried egg and white Jasmine rice. Meh. This restaurant has been voted in the Nashville Scene as Best Thai, but the only ones who vote on these surveys are the same group of people every year who live in their bubble they perceive as Nashville. There is so much more to Nashville than what the Nashville Scene chooses to display. Best Thai in Nashville? Far from it. Location - Good. Service - Great. Parking - Good. Quality - Great. Food - Fair. Authenticity - Questionable. Pricing - Fair. So our overall first impression of the Smiling Elephant is this: Although the owners may be Thai or Lao, they cater to the area and its market. Their menu says "not Americanized" but to us it is just that. They have altered some of their items to meet the needs of a gluten-free or low-carb diets. This may be good for people on those diets, but not for people who want a simple, authentic meal. Don't get me wrong - the food was not horrible, it just wasn't what we expected. I will say it again - the food is way overpriced. Maybe we should give it another chance and try more of their menu items, but I highly doubt that will happen anytime soon.
llm_rationale: No described illness, contamination, or unsafe food handling.

text: As a Cuban-American, I was excited to hear that St. Louis once again had a place to go for Cuban food. I understand that this is more of a Dominican restaurant instead of a Cuban or Puerto Rican restaurant, but there is some cross-over in cuisine with distinguishing features for each country. The mofongo is good here, and a sure thing. The Cuban sandwich is quite good and I have had it twice. The tostones and maduros are also great. Ropa vieja--fair at best. We were asked by the manager how we liked our meal, my husband (who--like I--is one of those people who cannot stand cilantro--even the smallest sprig makes an entire dish taste like dish soap) expressed that he did not enjoy his rope vieja because he did not expect to find cilantro in it. The snarky reply from the manager was "we're Dominican" and he walked away. Fine...but don't call it rope vieja. Call it Dominican carne ripiada or Dominican Ropa Vieja, but don't tell a Cuban that it is OK to contaminate our national dish with the offensive herb. Rude. Needless to say, I did not ask if they made Cuban coffee, and we asked for our check. I guess Mi Caribe is not my cup of Caribe and we will probably not return.

text: First Impressions: The entry looks quite upscale, prompting my partner to feel underdressed (he wasn't). Inside, the tall ceilings and wood panelling continued the impression with comfortable, inviting booths. There were a few ubiquitous pop culture posters on the walls; not enough to detract from the setting, but enough that I found them amusing. Can't find a casual restaurant nowadays that doesn't sport Marilyn's image. Atmosphere: While the decor was pleasant enough, the TV screens everywhere ruined the general effect. I don't mind them in a casual bar, but I don't understand their purpose in a dining room. The background music was decidedly Muzak, but it was quiet, so I didn't mind. Even as the place filled up, the sound level remained reasonable and we couldn't hear the conversations of other patrons. Menu: Reasonable selection for omnis and vegs alike with gluten-free pasta available for a surcharge (of course...). Veg items are not marked, but the server assured me that they could work with most of the dishes. Prices were comparable to other casual restaurants. Wine list: Not particularly varied, but enough for the average person to find accompaniment for their meal. Food: We started with the Arancini, deep-fried risotto balls. The menu didn't mention that they contained mushrooms; I wouldn't have ordered them had it said so. They came on a bed of wilted lettuce with a dollop of a delicious sauce on each. They weren't bad at all, if a little boring. And I hate mushrooms. My partner had this to say about his Penne Polo Alfredo ($17.95): "It was thin - milky rather than creamy. The pasta was cooked appropriately, but there wasn't much flavour and I had to work to coat each piece with sauce. I coulda got better at Boston Pizza." For my part, the Cannelloni ($15.95) was certainly palatable, if a little bland. I appreciated the sparing use of cheese in the filling, but the shells were over-cooked and the sauce lacked interest. For the price, I'd've been much happier at Sicilian Kitchen. Service: Our server was quite gracious, but she was also very busy. Perhaps they hadn't expected the rush? I'm not sure, but, well... We were prepared to order dessert, but it took so long for her to return to our table that we gave up and paid our bill instead. She also ignored my request for the 5oz glass of wine, neglected to clarify the size required by my partner, and brought us 8oz each. I didn't quibble with the bill, as we did drink the wine, but I do prefer a smaller glass with my meal. All in all, my partner and I agreed that, while we left full, we certainly weren't satisfied. I do appreciate the coupon with which we paid for my meal. I wouldn't've cared to pay full price for what we got. We likely won't return.
llm_rationale: No described illness, contamination, or unsafe food handling.

text: My husband and I were part of a party of six for dinner at Marzano, and my rating would be much higher were I only rating the food. But ambiance is also part of what makes a meal wonderful or awful or something in between. In this case I want to be specific and clear: The food was very, very good! But this was one of the noisiest restaurants I've experienced. Now, loud is, for some, a good thing. It can be interpreted as exciting, energetic, fun. Or--as in my case--it can be annoying, painful, disorienting. All six of us expressed some degree of concern about the deafening decibel level at Marzano, and four of us agreed we would not return because of it. If you like loud restaurants, then please try this one--and I mean that seriously, because the food was very good. I had a split avocado filled with a very elegant crab ceviche as an appetizer--just delightful! My companions enjoyed mussels in a very good, light tomato sauce, calamari (I'm not a fan, but my friend is and said it was great), a nice minestone and some big, fresh salads. all good! Our entrees included a special of orecchiette with shrimp, garden-fresh cherry tomatoes and broccoli rabe in a light olive oil/white wine sauce; risotta with an abundant mixture of seafood, rigatoni with Fra Daivolo and lasagna. No one at our table had anything to say but positives about their meals...or, possibly, I simply *could not hear* any negatives. It was that loud, what I think of "smile and nod" loud, where, after the meal, when you finally escape and walk outside, your ears still ringing, you wonder what you just agreed to while smiling and nodding. One final negative--if, like me, you are lactose intolerant, there will be no dessert for you...but how often is there? All the desserts here are cream-based. Now, why a restaurant cannot put some luscious cake under fresh fruit with the option of refusing whipped cream I do not understand. Perhaps this is a cultural thing and most Americans just want dairy-rich desserts, I do not know. Nor will I fault Mazano on this score because--as a majorly lactose intolerant girl--there rarely *is* dessert for me unless I am at home. So, in summary: very good food that could cross that fine line into *great* food, if you could enjoy your meal without the headache of loud, deafening, relentless, my-ears-still-ring-an-hour-later noise. If that will not bother you, go! If it will bother you, also go, but go on a warm summer evening and insist on a table outside. Yeah, it will overlook a parking lot. And yet, you will be able to hear what your friends say, and not be reduced to smiling and nodding aimlessly...and agreeing to, who knows what.

When there is a legitimate reason to ask that a service animal be removed, staff must offer the person with the disability the opportunity to obtain goods or services without the animal's presence. Establishments that sell or prepare food must allow service animals in public areas even if state or local health codes prohibit animals on the premises. People with disabilities who use service animals cannot be isolated from other patrons, treated less favorably than other patrons, or charged fees that are not charged to other patrons without animals. In addition, if a business requires a deposit or fee to be paid by patrons with pets, it must waive the charge for service animals. text: A Restaurant Week Review: First thing I thought when I walked into Supper... "Cool." The decor was very unique and suave. I don't think anyone would disagree on that. I couldn't stop looking around the place at all the awesome decor. Make sure to take a good look at the way cool "recycled" chandelier near the front door. Unfortunately the atmosphere was the more memorable part of the evening. Though rich in flavor, the food left a bit to be desired... I started off with the Black Truffle Deviled Eggs. I was so disappointed! The flavor was just blah and boring; too much mustard. They also tasted like they were made yesterday. Had that sitting-out-for-a-while texture. I really think this was due to the "high demands" of restaurant week and the eggs were made in bulk at some point and refrigerated. But still. Then I tried my dinner mates Housemade Soft Pretzels with green chile-and-beer fondue. The pretzels were yummy. But the sauce just tasted like plain ol' nacho cheese. Guess I just expected too much... For the "small plate" I ordered the Smoked Butternut Squash Soup with cinnamon marshmallow, apples and sage. YUM. After the 1st course I was kind of nervous for this one. But I certainly was pleasantly pleased with what came to me! Not only was the presentation awesome, the flavors and textures all worked so well together. Make sure to get the cinnamon marshmallow goodness off the side of the bowl and into each delightful spoonful! As for my "large plate", I went with the Vinegar Braised Chicken with figs, smoked bacon, anson mills grits and brussels sprouts. When in doubt, go with the chicken. That's what my father always told me and I'm glad I followed his advice. The chicken was super moist and the braise was phenomenal. However it was a major bummer getting bites of cartilage in there... But attention grits fans! I'm sure these would be some of the best grits you've ever tried. Normally I hate grits; bland, gritty, nasty... Supper's grits were so creamy and flavorful. Definitely lots of butter :) The brussel sprouts weren't half bad either! (On a side note... I thought my dinner mates Pork Loin was WAY too salty) Then came dessert and I got the Warm Apple Cobbler with biscuit topping and spiced whipped cream. I thought it was too bitter for my standards... And the whipped cream just tasted like fluffy milk. The best part was the biscuit. Monty Python would of been pleased... Dessert menu changes: It might of only been tonight, but the Olive Oil Sponge Cake wasn't on the menu. Instead they offered a "cookie plate" served with a chocolate egg cream. However they don't note anywhere that one of the cookies is peanut butter. So if you're allergic be careful! Cocktails... B-/C+ My Mandarin cocktail was supper refreshing. But my friends London Lou tasted like pure alcohol. As for service... A+ Our waiter was very friendly and efficient. Tried to crack a joke every now and then too. Overall I don't think Supper is the best choice, food wise, for restaurant week. But if you're one of those people who love a way cool atmosphere and being able to enjoy a rather somewhat pricey restaurant for a "good deal" during restaurant week... then be my guest!

text: My girlfriend and I went here tonight on a Groupon deal. Having never been here before, we were excited to be getting a chance to have some Greek food on the cheap. And actually, the meal started out really well. We ordered the Salata Caprese appetizer -- alternating layers of baked feta cheese and tomatoes on top of a bit of pesto with a dusting of dried oregano. The pesto was a bit on the tame side and the tomatoes reminded us that it is winter after all, but overall we really liked it. The trouble started when the waitress asked us for our entree order. My girlfriend has a gluten intolerance and can't have anything with wheat, so we asked our waitress what we should look at. She ruled out the pita bread and the pasta, as well as anything that came on a bun or had filo dough in it. I added, "And anything with bechamel, right?" She looked perplexed, and said that bechamel is a cheese sauce so we shouldn't worry. Now, having made bechamel before myself, I can tell you that a basic bechamel sauce is made from three ingredients: butter, flour, and cream. Accordingly, I expressed some hesitation, but she insisted. I told her that if she could make absolutely sure that the bechamel sauce did not have any flour in it, then we would have an order of the bechamel-topped moussaka, as well as the braised lamb shank in red sauce. Upon consulting the kitchen, she returned to tell us that indeed, the bechamel did have flour in it. One of the kitchen staff got her attention, however, and apparently told her that they had made a mistake: the bechamel would be safe -- they had looked at the list of ingredients. Perhaps needless to say, when the moussaka came out, it was immediately clear to me that it had flour in it, just like normal bechamel does (or perhaps I am wrong, in which case I have no idea what they're serving people under the guise of bechamel sauce). It was okay -- I just gave my girlfriend the lamb and we were on our way. Unfortunately, neither dish was that great. The moussaka was a pretty standard example of its kind, but it wasn't particularly well-seasoned and didn't impress me with its flavor. It came with some decent potatoes, some veggies that didn't really have much to distinguish them, and some straightforward rice pilaf. The lamb came with the same sides, but it wasn't the highest-quality meat and the red sauce was unrefined -- too acidic and not well-suited to the lamb. When we were finished, we asked about dessert and found out that we couldn't get the only gluten free one on the menu because they had run of yogurt (at a Greek restaurant!). Ultimately, this wasn't a nightmare experience or anything like that. Our waitress was actually really friendly, and although the food wasn't great, it's not like we found a severed toe in it (actually, my girlfriend pulled a hair out of her mouth at one point, but it could definitely have been mine). The restaurant itself was attractive and well-kept, the portion sizes were good, and the menu hit on all the standards. It's just that the food wasn't very good, and the staff clearly had no idea what they were actually serving people -- a pretty gravely bad sign in my book. Given the other perfectly-good Greek options in Tucson (particularly Opa! for this level of dining), I just would advise looking elsewhere.
llm_rationale: No described illness, contamination, or unsafe food handling.

text: Regrub is one of those places you really, really want to love. It's new, it's been trendy somewhere else (Calgary), it's colorful, its menu is full of funny names, and it's convenient to the Whyte Ave walking stretch of pavement. I was excited to "drop a pin" into this nouveau burger experience, doubly so with a bit of the hangry. So the other half did the ordering while I soaked in the ambiançe: it's like the Teletubbies grew up to high school, got to plan a menu, decorate a space, pick a soundtrack and make social media accounts. Yeah, it's like that. That part is all good. It's a fun, colorful space with happy, shiny staff. The fail parts are the execution of the food and the value-for-money propositions. Those could use a lot of tweaking. She wanted the Lutter, a 4 oz Alberta Beef patty with bacon, egg, and cheddar surrounded by a bun of split glazed donuts. I liked the contrast of the sweet and savoury, whereas the 'bunny felt the donut didn't meet up to her Tim Horton'y expectations. (It tasted to me like a Krispy Kreme regular glazed donut, FYI.) The Cheesy Jr., a 4 oz patty topped with mac n' cheese with bacon bits, arrived looking (seriously) like those Halloween caricatures of a pumpkin vomiting out its insides. Yes, there's pale creamy pasta with bits covering most of the serving tray... in a competition, this contestant would have been sent home. It's a presentation that screams "I'm so drunk I can't even bother looking for flatware. I'm using my hands and lots of paper towels." Still, it's the taste that counts (mostly) but this explosion wasn't rescued: it was under-salted and nowhere as cheesy as it *needed* to be. My ultimate measure of a restaurant's worth to me comes down to whether it (1) delivers a food that I can't easily make at home along with (2) an experience that's memorable at (3) a rationalizable price. Regrub fails on the former; I can whip up dorm-quality meat patties & KD without any effort. The middle; okay, interesting location slash vibe slash space. The latter; meh. Everyone felt mugged. The worst thing of all? This is *so* close to executing well. Krikey, taste the damn food on the way out of the kitchen! Tighten up food design and assembly; try to be impressing someone... Oh, and your Instagram counter behind the till is broken. Even that narcissistic rush doesn't work. Meh.
llm_rationale: No described illness, contamination, or unsafe food handling.

text: I'm a reluctant, ambivalent Epic regular. A recent move places Epic as the closest cafe, and rapidly approaching finals coupled with an uncanny caffeine addiction drag me into this oddly eclectic and contradictory place. Hours: Open until midnight every night. Awesome. WIFI: The internet is more consistent and faster than at either Bentley's or Caffe Luce. It's less reliable but faster than Starbucks. It's less reliable and slower than Crave, UMC cafeteria, Raging Sage, Cartel, etc. Staff: I've interacted with nearly every staff member at this point. I haven't been the overly-friendly, open person I typically am - but even with that, all of the staff have been quite friendly. I'm a fairly observant individual and occasionally I'm here for 10 hours at a time - I've never observed them treat anyone poorly. I have observed them go out of their way to help people though. I like them. Coffee: The price is about the same as most other coffee shops, as is the quality. In my biased opinion, nothing has come close to matching Ike's in quality or price, and I lament daily over this tragic loss. Food: Over-priced, but tasty. It's on par with Bentley's ridiculous prices. They have a wide variety of freshly baked goods that vary by the day. As another reviewer has attested, the breakfast burrito is phenomenal - but again, paying $6.00 for a tortilla, potatoes and eggs is absurd - but hey, I'm an absurd person, so bring on some more egregiously priced burritos. Cleanliness: Many have commented on unsanitary conditions. There are flies buzzing about on occasion, sure; and the bathrooms - although I wouldn't call them a disaster - are vile in an aesthetic sense. I wouldn't consider them any less sanitary than any other coffee shop bathroom - it's just the aesthetics. Personally, I derive some grotesque sort of solace from the witty, inappropriate commentary scribbled over the bathroom walls. The furniture...it does seem a bit dingy, but that's what gives this place character. You want sterile? Go to Starbucks, you drone. Patrons: Diverse. College students, professors, graduate students, hipsters, yuppies, retired folk, indigents, etc. Unlike my vast experiences at Coffee Xchange, I've never witnessed an "event" here where shit gets cray cray. No bums throwing chairs and screaming about murdering everyone. No methed out college kids trying to guzzle down 6 red-eyes in one go while loudly shouting about how dark it is outside when it's 2am in the morning. No heavy drug use in the bathrooms (that I'm aware of, although it's likely, because people are awesome like that). Overall, it's safe here. If you're afraid of being exposed to peculiar individuals, crawl back into your hole or stick to Starbucks drive-thrus. On a personal note, I find it exceptionally odd that they so heavily push "gluten-free" foods, are a certified "green business," etc., yet they sell cigarettes here. This hipster element fills me with contempt. Further, the little spiritual / meditation / new age / snake oil pamphlet/books they have for sale near the window makes me shudder in disdain. Overall, I love and hate this place. It's comfortable in an uncomfortable way. The staff is great, the food is good, and the coffee is average. The prices can go jump off a bridge and die. Ultimately, I mourn the loss of Ike's. Epic is a necessary supplement. If Ike's or its functional equivalent were to open anywhere in Tucson, I'd instantly abandon ship and find residence elsewhere, regardless of the bicycling mileage involved.
llm_rationale: No described illness, contamination, or unsafe food handling.

text: Copa is the Jekyll and Hyde of West Philly. By day, a humble outpost serving fine Mexican fare, and its sweet weekday deals beckon the wallet of the most frugal man, woman, and inexplicably mature child. The staff is Bueno (Spanish for good), and the flavors excellente (Spanish for excellent). But you're not here for the good doctor, are you? Of course not. You'd like to make the acquaintance of one Mr. Hyde. And so you shall. Any night Copa breathes a fire not unlike those you may have seen in a household fireplace. The bar is full, the tables overflowing. A collision of locals and university students, brought together by the allure of the famously mediocre margarita. The first sip greets your lips like an old friend. The second, like an old friend who you just remembered owes you money and has not paid you back in years. Enough money to be reasonably irked, but not quite enough to bring it up when you only see each other at weddings and birthdays, anyway. The rest goes not in sips, but gulps. Time slows, conversations slur, everything grows dark. Your friend stabs you with your epi pen and you come back to life. A novice mistake, you had a small helping of almonds before coming out with the boys. But your allergies don't stop you, no, Copa overcomes all. You pull yourself back onto the barstool and request a napkin from the bartender to apply pressure to your bloody skull while the bar tender shakes up your next marg. This one will be taken with nachos, because they keep the kitchen open late - - a class act. This is the good life. I have some beef with Copa, albeit only two very thin slices. Slice number one is that there is nowhere to dance, yet the bastards have the audacity to play a bumping set. Slice number two is that they charge a small cover when you're just trying to get in there to give them your money anyway. A good business practice or a slap in the face of bona fide American democracy? I leave this as an exercise to the reader.
llm_rationale: Reviewer had an allergic reaction after consuming food at Copa, requiring an EpiPen.

I was starving so there was no way I was sending it back at this point and so, I trudged on and chewed through the meat like a dog chewing on rawhide. I was extremely disappointed. No flavor, just the taste of burnt beef in my mouth. And let's not even get into the brioche bun being used yet again in a completely unoriginal attempt to fancy-ify this overpriced bar burger. ($11?? Seriously??) Regardless of how busy your kitchen is, the least you can do is try to prepare food to your customer's request. I can only imagine what would have happened if I ordered a steak there (if they even serve steak; I have no clue.) Or if I had some kind of food allergy. I guess they just figured it was better to overcook my burger then undercook it, and that does not a good burger make. Bad dog, very bad dog.
llm_rationale: Reviewer's burger was overcooked despite requesting medium, and they experienced an allergic reaction to the aioli.

text: This is certainly one of my new favorite restaurants in the city. I had a 7pm reservation on a Tuesday night for me and my friend who was visiting from Canada. She just recently moved out of Philly and when deciding where to go for dinner, her only request was for me to choose a place that was new for both of us. Spice Finch had been on my mind for a few months now so I figured this would be perfect for the occasion. Our sweet waitress gave us a rundown of the menu and told us that dishes are typically made for sharing. With that in mind, we both ordered fries to share but decided to choose our own entrees. I'm allergic to both chickpeas and lentils so unfortunately, I have quite a few food restrictions at Mediterranean restaurants. I shared this with the waitress when I ordered the peri-peri shrimp and she assured me that she would speak to the chef to make sure these ingredients were not used in this dish and there was no cross contamination. Thank you to the team at Spice Finch for making me feel so well taken care of! The peri-peri shrimp was incredible. So flavorful and rich with well-cooked, plump shrimp. I became a huge fan of peri peri during my trip to South Africa last year and am so happy I got to enjoy it here. The dish came with a side of buttery flatbread that I dipped into the sauce. The fries that my friend and I shared were also very good. They were well-seasoned and the portion was huge. I couldn't have the hummus aioli they come with but my friend said it was delicious. Although the sauce looked great, I was more than content just enjoying the fries sans dip! For dessert we enjoyed a slice of chocolate cake with tahini soufflé and blood orange sorbet. I was a little skeptical because I'm not usually a fan of fruity desserts but wow was this dish really something! The blood orange sorbet really balanced out the rich chocolate cake, but in my opinion, the tahini soufflé was the MVP. I could have eaten spoonfuls of that alone! The restaurant is beautiful. It is open and airy with the appropriate lighting. It isn't too bright but not too dark either. Lighting can make such a big difference - it really sets the mood and Spice Finch does it just right. This restaurant is great for get-togethers, celebrations or dates. I can't wait to return here. I'm tempted to make my next experience a brunch outing, but with such an incredible dinner, it'll be hard not to go back for that!
llm_rationale: The reviewer mentions a food allergy but no adverse event occurred.

text: From wallpapered walls on which spotlit photos of homes are hung, to plain brick facade, to large blown-up portraits of Joplin, Hendrix, and other classic rockers, Twisted Tail's lower level is somewhat confusing. This confusion extends to the kitchen, wherein the recent chef switcheroo of Michael Stevenson for Leo Forneas has led to the restaurant's refocus from the pure Southern bourbon and blues motif that previously and not very successfully defined them since opening a few years ago. On a normal day, this would be enough in itself, but I chose to visit during Mother's Day, pretty much the worst day for dining out, especially when you're part of a party of eight. So the service, while not bad, per se, gets a pass. What doesn't get a pass is the prix fixe menu from which we were forced to order. The menu consisted of literally every item of their normal brunch menu, plus a couple of desserts, for a significantly higher price than normal. So say you wanted to order the salad and buttermilk chicken sandwich - $15 on a normal Sunday. $35 on Mother's Day. But you got a choice of beignets or panna cotta for dessert, so I'm sure that warranted the extra markup. Needless to say, I made it a priority to choose the absolute most expensive things on their normal brunch menu. Another problem with just throwing your entire menu onto a prix fixe is portion sizes. My tuna tartare was simply mixed with the occasional sliced cornichon and served alongside a few potato chips, but it was fresh and a good size to prime to palate for the rest of the meal. Some of my fellow diners got the pigs in a blanket, which were nearly a main course in themselves. After plowing through a few of them, multiple people remarked at how full they were getting, and the main course hadn't even arrived yet. The Maryland Crab cake eggs benedict isn't what you'd expect to find in a Southern-slanted restaurant, but I'm glad it's here, because the crab cakes were almost all crab, and went really well with the eggs (poached well for me, though others weren't so lucky), mustard hollandaise, and English muffin. Serving them alongside french fries seemed like they just didn't want to take the time to prepare an additional starch, and I didn't want to take the time to eat the underwhelming slices of potato. Fried dough is an easy crowd pleaser, and the beignets hit the spot, even if they were still a little doughy. The gluten-free diner amongst us described her panna cotta as "interesting," and not in a good way, though she seemed unfamiliar with the dish. To be honest, the combination of food and company provided an overall positive experience at Twisted Tail, though there were enough missteps to not make it a priority to return. Regardless of the good service from our server, and the great service from the managers in seating us in what must have been a hellish time for them, the food still needs a little bit of refinement.

We put in our order and waited. and waited. A waiter made two trips to bring things to our table. Neither of which were ours. I tried the wonton fried shrimp. I'd had it before and remembered it fondly. Never again. The shrimp, unlike the ones in the picture were small, grey and anemic looking. The wontons instead of spread over were dumped in one corner as if someone remember just as the plate was going out the door and threw a handful after the retreating platter. Even worse, the stir fried vegetables were burned, blackened even. I started to make a mound of the inedible, charred bits on the side of the plate but it was just too many, the rice was dotted with tiny charred bits of pepper and broccoli and trying them, hoping the sauce would smoother the flavor, was a mistake. It was just foul. I left almost all of it on the plate. At NO point did the server ask how was the meal, even when done and I asked for the check, there seemed no interest in what experience their customer had. As I said this Applebee's had been a favorite just to go out casually. It has been degrading with increasingly poor service over the last few months but it's hit rock bottom now. with inattentive and slow servers and food that is just flat out bad.

text: I was super excited to try this place after a friend raved about them. We called ahead and made a reservation for the same night, Saturday night. The stuffed jalapeño appetizer was strange in temperature, it is deep fried but its cold and the jalapeño is raw. It was a weird temperature experience, wouldn't order again. The 3 of us ordering AYCE ordered a total of 7 rolls to start. We typically eat about 3 rolls per person, but started w 7. The ordering is not similar to others in town, as they come to the table to order, instead of giving you paper to write down. Half of our rolls came on one plate, with appropriate portioned rice. The other half came with 2x the rice of the original plate. Wayyy too much rice. They also brought us out 8 rolls, not just the 7 that we ordered. 5 of our rolls included shrimp, which is what ultimately ruined our experience. The shrimp was not good, a very rubbery texture. The shrimp were huge, not easy to eat with the excess rice portions. Remember, they also brought us extra food that we didn't order. And their rolls are HUGE even without the extra rice.. the rolls were not edible, they were rubbery and ricey. Of the 7 rolls we ordered, they brought 8... and we ate as much as we could stomach... leaving less than 3 rolls to waste. As a business...seeing over 30% waste, this should have prompted the staff to ask why we weren't eating our rolls. But they didn't. They asked if we wanted a to-go box. We told them no, no to-go box, and advised that it didn't taste good and that they'd also brought us food more food than we ordered. Despite being honest with our dissatisfaction, we were charged an excess waste fee. Technically we ordered less food than cost effective for AYCE.... even with appetizers, we would have saved probably $10 if we had done ala carte. We honestly expected the rolls to be edible and expected to eat more. I was really blown away that they would charge the waste fee after we voiced out dissatisfaction, the small amount of food we actually ordered, and that I've never actually been charged that fee anywhere (but I have never had rubbery gross shrimp in all my rolls before either.) I was really bummed by the inconsistency w rolls & rice portion, and lack of interest in what we thought of the food quality. I wish we had started with some non-shrimp rolls so we may have had a more pleasant dining experience. Everything else seemed to taste very fresh. My rating would have been a 3/4 if it hadn't been for the waste charge.

text: Everything was good here except for the one thing that really, really matters to me: cleanliness. If it weren't for that I would have given this place five stars. My water glass looked a little dirty, but I decided to not make a big deal out of it. I've worked in a restaurant before and I know that sometimes hard water stains can make a glass look dirty even if it's perfectly clean. Then, I unwrapped my silverware. There was food still crusted on my fork. My knife looked like it had water stains or it was just plain dirty. I grabbed the silverware from the table next to mine. The fork was clean, but the knife was dirty. I also noticed that our server saw me doing this and saw the extra dirty silverware on our table, but never mentioned it or asked about it. I have a feeling this has happened before. The only reason I didn't get up and leave was because we had already ordered all our food and the appetizer had been brought out to us. Actually, mostly it was because we were just extremely tired. Like, so tired you feel drunk and not willing to walk around looking for another restaurant tired. You better believe I inspected every single bite of food. Luckily, it seemed like the plates were clean and the food looked ok. Finally, the bathrooms looked like the ones straight out of a club around 2am on a Friday night. Dark, dingy, and dirty. Now, I'm kind of grossed out that I ate here since who knows how clean the kitchen is, but at least the food tasted good. Also, I was fully expecting to get food poisoning but I was perfectly fine.

text: I'm not judging this Boston Market as much as I'm judging Boston Market as a company (aka I'm totally judging their menu items). When the cashier at the normal line was done checking out a couple, she called me over and got my food! The food preparer read out my order and that was an added bonus. She printed my receipt (which has a coupon on it!) and wished me a happy day! The inside looked pretty clean and was pretty empty. Now, onto my actual order. The chicken was bomb dot com. The sauce? As delicious as I remember. The perfect amount of spice. The mac and cheese is as good as I remember it to be. Not too cheesy but enough to make me want more! And the cornbread. Good lord, the cornbread! My mom makes the best cornbread, and while BM's cornbread definitely isn't the best, something about it is addicting. I'm not sure how I limited myself to one piece. Two MAJOR disappoints? The steamed veggies and that damn squash casserole (aka vomit). The steamed veggies tasted like they were steamed in garbage water. They had this odd taste to them and were definitely not seasoned with anything. I managed to get most of the broccoli and zucchini/green beans down (by dipping them in the cheese sauce) but those carrots were so hard I didn't even bother! I would definitely recommend just getting a freaking SteamFresh bag of veggies at Publix instead of getting this as a side. I have had several types of casseroles in the past, and they've all been pretty good. This one? It was bad. Not only did it look SO unappetizing, it didn't taste like anything! It looked like I was eating vomit, the consistency was horrible, and it just had no freaking flavor. I don't even know how else to explain it, but seriously, please opt out, unless of course you like eating barf. Then, by all means, go ahead! Also, there's a $1.50 off of $10 coupon online! You can apply it to your online order.

I don't know that I'll be back soon as I'm very disappointed in the deviation from the menu as listed. Another big thing is that you changed something and didn't even consider I may have an allergy and many other things. text: I really wanted to like Raz'z. I really did. But they didn't make it easy. My husband and I stopped here before a movie about 6:30 on a Tuesday night, and the atmosphere was great--business casual, with several tables filled with what looked like after-work dinners or business meetings. The room was lit dimly and each table had a candle. I felt a little underdressed in my jeans, but soon noticed a few other patrons wearing similar attire so I relaxed. As a vegetarian I was happy to see several options available to me, including a vegetarian pasta, a veggie burger and, sadly on Fridays only, a vegetarian lasagna. I opted for the vegetarian pasta al fresca and my husband ordered the beef lasagna. But then, trouble started. As he was eating his house salad, my husband discovered he was chewing on a shrimp tail--and he's very allergic to shrimp. Then, as he was eating his lasagna, he not only pulled out several pieces of gristle but an inch-long piece of what appeared to be plastic. My pasta al fresca, which was described as including a "medley of vegetables," only had broccoli and carrots, which were undercooked and almost impossible to bite through. The chef and our server apologized for the shrimp incident, although they were conflicted as to how it could have happened (our server told us seafood and lettuce are chopped in separate areas of the kitchen and never come in contact; the chef told us they are both chopped side-by-side next to the sink). We weren't upset, just a little surprised and wanted to bring it to the server's attention, but they both were very apologetic. As an apology, our server offered us a complimentary walnut-brownie dessert, but unfortunately my husband doesn't eat walnuts. She didn't offer up any of their other desserts instead, so I accepted the brownie. I'd like to say it ended happily, but the brownie was so hard I would have had to use my knife if I wanted to eat most of it. I ate as much as I could, and we decided to cut our losses and leave. It's unfortunate that we had a bad experience at a restaurant with such a great menu, cool atmosphere and friendly wait staff, because I would have loved to have been able to leave them a great review. At this point, I'm not sure if we're going to return. One problem with the food is enough, but finding shrimp tails, gristle and plastic all in the same meal seems like a symptom of a larger issue.
llm_rationale: Reviewer's husband had a severe allergic reaction to shrimp in his meal.

text: So every Sunday, my mom and I goto brunch after church. Usually we goto the Cheesecake Factory because their omelet portion is HUGE and we just share it. She did warn us there would be a wait if we went between 10am-1pm on the weekend - we showed up around 11:15 or so, and yes, we waited. And waited. AND waited. We were told 35 minutes, that turned into 1 1/2 hours. This place is SMALL. And the crowd is BIG. The wait is LONG. And you can't sit at the bar, or anywhere if you're waiting. You basically stand. It's like being at a college bar, it's crowded! While waiting, my mom had coffee and really enjoyed it - the coffee is rather inexpensive too. I had some green tea, pretty good. We were finally seated - at the high top table, which is wobbly. So are the chairs. I was scared mine was going to break, it was that wobbly. There was a group of 5 people standing next to our table CONSTANTLY bumping our table making it shake, it was beyond annoying. Especially for my mom who was sitting at the end of the table, and the table was nailing her in her chest and stomach. We ordered the cali omelet and asked for brussels sprouts to be added & light on the cheese (I'm lactose intolerant) - it came with house potatoes and toast, we had whole wheat. While waiting, we started with some mixed fruit, which was really fresh. Comes with homemade whip cream - yum. Our omelet comes out - Looked good, lots of avocado, etc. Well, I had to send it back because it was LOADED with cheese. So we send it back.... It comes back, a little light on the cheese, but then while eating it - We notice: 1. NO black beans 2. NO brussels sprouts 3. Didn't get our toast back 4. MUCH less avocado So basically this omelet was a plain omelet with nothing in it that it is supposed to acquire. So we sent it back (embarrassingly) - 3 times a charm right? This time, the chef brings it out, and it was done how it was supposed to be done. I usually don't complain about food because I'm not picky, but when it concerns my health, I got to... And the fact it came out TWICE not correct - that's not good. This place as a lot of hype. Other dishes looked pretty good though, I will admit. But having to wait THAT long and having to return our food TWICE, wasn't a pleasant first time visit here. If you do come here, come early, or come during the week. Or else you'll be standing and waiting for a very very long time. The building is entirely too small for the big crowd that it seems to attract. I suggest expanding, something, and adding a small area of chairs or couches where people can wait, because everyone standing around and BUMPING our table consistently is quite annoying.
