Throughout our time there, our waiter was slammed and rarely checked on us with refills, requested items, etc. We had to remind him for things we asked for before receiving them (ie forks, refills, etc) The forks that we received upon request were plastic mind you, so they were practically worthless against the crab legs that we needed them for. Now, that Negative Nancy has made her appearance, let's invite Positive Polly to the review. The food was great! I ordered off the a la carte menu as my date didn't want to share meal-for-two smh. I had a pound of crab legs, a pound of shrimp, one corn on the cob, and one order of potatoes (a pack of three). I got these with the "whole shebang" seasoning and mild temperature. It was all delicious! I especially loved the corn! It was great and well prepared.The mild temperature still had a kick to it. For my drink I had the peach tea, which was really tasty! My date had the "middle" pre-fixe meal. I don't remember the name of it, but it came with crab legs, shrimp, crawfish, potatoes, sausages, and corn. He got this with the "whole shebang" seasoning, and medium temperature. He really enjoyed everything! I had some sausage from his meal and it was delicious! The medium was definitely hotter than the mild, which again was still spicy. This was no cheap feast, but it was about what you'd expect for a seafood boil in St. Louis (expect around $30-$40 a person depending on what you plan on adding to it). Now, I'd be remiss if I didn't add that my date was sick the next day with a stomach bug. He told me that he woke up at 5am the next day vomiting and it continued all day. I did not get sick at all. I repeat, I DID NOT GET SICK AT ALL! So I can't say that it was from something that he ate or not. Granted, we ate out of two different boil bags, although I still had a couple crawfish and sausages from his bag and wasn't sick at all. I just thought I'd share that because it was the last meal he ate prior to getting sick.
llm_rationale: Reviewer's date got sick with a stomach bug the next day after eating at the restaurant.

text: I ordered some takeout online and received one of the worst Sushi orders I've ever picked up. So many things were wrong with my order: 1) They did not follow any of the special instructions. They weren't crazy instructions either, just "do not include this ingredient." Why bother to have a special instructions field if you don't read it? Don't order online if you have allergies, I guess. 2) They got one item completely wrong. This wasn't a close thing, either: I ordered Mackerel (Saba) and received Squid (Ika). Those aren't even vaguely similar. 3) Said Squid was BAD. I don't mean low quality, I mean it was spoiled, and if you've ever had the misfortune of eating spoiled squid you know how dangerous that can be. If you haven't... out both ends, for hours. 4) Their veggie "assortment" for tempura consists entirely of potato (not sweet potato, plain potato) and zucchini. The tempura batter itself was not good quality and had trouble sticking to the veggies, especially the zucchini. 5) The rice in their sushi was mushy and bland, exceptionally so. It brought the already mediocre quality of the sushi down even more. I really did not expect something this bad given all the other good reviews of this place. I don't know if they're having issues due to the pandemic or what, but I won't be ordering from this place again.
llm_rationale: Reviewer described eating spoiled squid that caused a potentially dangerous food poisoning incident.

text: Oh man. I really hate writing these kind of reviews - especially for smaller businesses trying to make it in this world - but I also believe if you are going to make it, you have to do what you do and do it well. We called at 7:45 and asked if we made it by 8:30, could they serve us. They said yes, they do not close until 9. We arrived at 8:20 and they refused to seat us. Said they were closing. The place had one other table and I am guessing they just wanted to leave - but we made a special trip after working all day and were starving. They finally relented and sat us. We tried to be really nice and be good customers and order quickly, etc. They continued to be unfriendly. The food was mediocre and being a vegetarian, I ordered the chile paneer dish - which I will admit was good, but I ended up really sick later on that night. I really do have this feeling that it was cross contaminated with the lamb and chicken dishes my friends ordered - which I know can happen, but it would be great if kitchens, especially ethnic ones that tout vegetarian dishes, would be more aware of this issue. The Naan basket, which is my favorite part of eating Indian, was soggy and not very flavorful. All and all, we didn't have a good time and will not be going back when we are in town for work next.

text: This review is long over due, but worth the effort! If you're in the area, this joint is a must, but only for their food. My family and I came here on a Sunday about two weeks ago and the facility was only so-so busy. Our waitress (who seemed experienced) was not the most pleasant. Her attitude was very snarky and known-it-all, but not helpful the least. It's ranch!" Needless to say, her ability to serve went down hill from here and fast. She wouldn't help me find something on the menu that Accommodated my allergies. If the food wasn't so stinking good, I would not want to return due to the poor service. I was and still am super disappointed in the service there. text: My quest for Indy's best tacos takes me to the place that's all the rage, Indy Tacos. With a name like Indy Tacos, I suppose you know what you are getting yourself into. The location certainly takes me out of my Carmel comfort zone. My partner and I ordered 4 tacos (together, not each. That would be considered obesity to many). I got the fish and the carne asada (steak). The fish was a REEL CATCH. No, really. It was super tasty. I don't know what the fish is and I sure know it's not fresh. But the mixture of the lightly breaded shrimp with the slaw on top was super flavorful. This isn't a San Diego fish taco - this is a street fish taco. The steak taco was fine and the salsa was a helpful addition. I went with the green as red generally scares me. As a read head, you've got to know when there is too much of a good thing so I steer clear of red food. He got the mango chicken and while I don't recall his specific sentiment, but I don't remember medically induced vomit or an impromptu quinceanera so we will assume it was average. The staff are awesome, plenty of parking, and Jarritos for all (assuming you pay, which they most certainly encourage). Best so far in Indy if you count legit, real-deal Mexican taqueria (which rules out Bakersfield).
llm_rationale: No described illness or contamination, just a humorous and subjective review of the food.

text: Wow, I used to really like coming here but the quality and availability of ingredients and the cleanliness of this location had made this visit my last.
